subject: On-prem deployment: K8s assembly floorplan & compact blockstore schedule
messages:
From: Ellie Park <ellie.park@edgeworks.net>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ops@datafoundry.io
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Ops kickoff - site inventory & schedule for compact blockstore

Hi Hannah / Laura,

Thanks for taking this on. We're finalising the floorplan for the initial on-site roll (two racks) and need a compact, production-safe plan that fits our constrained footprint. High-level asks:

- Confirm node class sizing for model-serving (L, M) and batch/ingest worker pools.
- PV binding strategy for GPU pods + small fast blockstore for KV cache (nvme-attached preferred).
- Fallback storage plan if local NVMe is insufficient (networked iSCSI/Ceph).
- Timeline: hardware arrives 2029-05-02; we need a validated K8s layout and storage binding by 2029-04-22 to allow squash-testing.

Attached: site-inventory.csv (rack heights, PDU details). Can you propose a compact matrix (node counts, CPU/GPU, PV classes) we can share with the on-site team?

Thanks,
Ellie

--
Ellie Park
Head of Field Ops, EdgeWorks
ellie.park@edgeworks.net

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: Ellie Park <ellie.park@edgeworks.net>, ops@datafoundry.io
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ops kickoff - site inventory & schedule for compact blockstore

Ellie — thanks, received the inventory. Short version below; I attached a detailed node-class matrix (redwood-nodeclassmatrix.xlsx).

Proposed compact footprint (two-rack constraint):
- Control plane: 3x m5-large (dedicated, no GPUs), taint control-plane=true:NoSchedule
- Model-serving pool (L-profile): 4x g2-48 (1x A100-equivalent, 384GB RAM) — steady-state for 4 concurrent streams
- Inference pool (M-profile): 2x g1-24 (2 GPUs, 192GB RAM) for burst/batch fallback
- Worker/ingest: 2x c6-medium (cpu-only) for preprocessing and sidecar tasks

Storage binding recommendations:
- Local fast (nvme): use as ephemeral cache + KV disk (emptyDir backing to speedup) and a PersistentVolume local provisioner for a subset of pods that need local persistence.
- Network fallback: RBD/Ceph over 10Gb with LVM-backed PV class for model artifacts and longer-term checkpoints.
- PVC classes: pv-nvme-fast (no-reclaim: Retain), pv-network-standard (Retain), and pv-ephemeral (Delete) for scratch.

Encryption & keys: recommend customer KMS integration for PV encryption; we'll provide a KMS adapter for secrets only. If HSM is required for private keys, escalate now.

Timeline check: We can deliver the final validated layout and a kubeadm + iks bootstrap recipe by 2029-04-20 if we lock node counts by 2029-04-15.

Attachments: redwood-nodeclassmatrix.xlsx

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ops kickoff - site inventory & schedule for compact blockstore

Quick notes from infra:
- Agree with Hannah's split. Add two small changes:
  1) Offer a "compact-redundant" profile: 3x L-profile (instead of 4) + 1 spare node for faster failover in the rack-limited case. This reduces steady-state GPU capacity but gives better availability.
  2) Set PV reclaim policy to "Retain" for model artifacts; we will provide a post-maintenance manual scrub SOP.

- KV cache durability: don't rely on local NVMe for single-writer state. Instead, run a small clustered Redis backed by the network PV class with async replication — keeps warm cache and allows redis failover between racks.

Also adding action: Marissa will run a quick cost delta for compact-redundant vs nominal profile and share with DataFoundry ops by EOD.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

On Thu, Apr 11, 2029 at 10:45 AM hannah_schmitt@redwood.com wrote:
> Ellie — thanks, received the inventory. Short version below; I attached a detailed node-class matrix (redwood-nodeclassmatrix.xlsx).

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:
- Rack power is limited to 12kW per rack; we need exact per-node power draw estimates to confirm thermal margins. Can you include the per-node TDP in the matrix?
- HSM: our security team (Suresh) flagged that persistent keys must live in our on-prem HSM; can you confirm Redwood's KMS adapter supports external HSM via PKCS#11?
- Doc ask: can you produce a single-page "compact plan" that the on-site techs can follow (boot order, network VLAN allocation, PV class names, and basic smoke tests)?

We can accept the compact-redundant profile if you include the spare node and a short SLA note around model reload times (target < 90s for hot-swap).

Attachments requested: compact-blockstore-sla-v1.pdf (for our internal review)

Ellie

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: Ellie Park <ellie.park@edgeworks.net>, ops@datafoundry.io
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 13 Apr 2029 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ops kickoff - site inventory & schedule for compact blockstore

Ellie / team — finalising deliverables and next steps below.

Decisions agreed:
- Adopt "compact-redundant" profile: 3x L-profile GPU nodes + 1 spare node per rack (holds warm standby).
- PV classes: pv-nvme-fast (local), pv-network-standard (Ceph RBD over 10Gb), pv-ephemeral for scratch. Reclaim policy: Retain for network PVs.
- KV cache: small clustered Redis on pv-network-standard with replication across racks; local NVMe for ephemeral per-pod cache only.
- KMS/HSM: Redwood KMS adapter supports PKCS#11 + customer HSM configuration. Ops team to share HSM vendor docs and endpoint by 2029-04-16.

Action items & owners:
- Marissa: cost delta & OPEX impact (compact vs nominal) — due 2029-04-15.
- Laura: finalize kubeadm bootstrap playbook and VLAN tagging documentation — due 2029-04-18.
- Hannah & Vivek: deliver the site one-pager (boot checklist + smoke tests) and final nodeclass matrix — due 2029-04-20.
- DataFoundry: confirm HSM endpoint and per-node power limits (per-node TDP) by 2029-04-15.

I've attached the compact plan PDF (compact-blockstore-sla-v1.pdf) and the nodeclass matrix spreadsheet. If all looks good we'll schedule a pre-flight call 2029-04-21 with the on-site team.

Thanks everyone — closing this thread for decisions and next-step tracking.

Hannah
